annotations.description: Playing Swamp on turn 1 instead of Thriving Bluff wastes the opportunity to deploy the tapped land when there's nothing to cast. If Thriving Bluff is played turn 2 instead, it enters tapped and the player can't cast their 2-drop (Burglar Rat or Wight) on curve. If they play a second Swamp turn 2 instead, the Bluff gets delayed further.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp on turn 1 with no spells to cast
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Bluff on turn 1 (choosing black), then Swamp on turn 2 to cast Burglar Rat or Wight of Precinct Six on curve

annotations.description: Playing Thriving Bluff (enters tapped) instead of Swamp means the player has only 1 untapped mana this turn and cannot cast any of their three 2-mana creatures (Burglar Rat, Tinybones, Wight of Precinct Six). The hand is full of BB-cost cards and the red mana isn't needed anytime soon.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Thriving Bluff, leaving only 1 untapped mana and unable to cast a 2-drop this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp to have 2 untapped Swamps, enabling a turn-3 play like Burglar Rat (to set up Tinybones discard synergy) or Tinybones itself.

annotations.description: Playing Burglar Rat before Tinybones, Trinket Thief misses the synergy between the two cards. If Tinybones were on the battlefield when Burglar Rat enters, the opponent's discard would trigger Tinybones to draw a card at end step. By playing Burglar Rat first, this card draw is lost.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Burglar Rat on turn 5 without Tinybones on the battlefield
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tinybones, Trinket Thief this turn (after playing a land), then cast Burglar Rat next turn to trigger both the discard and Tinybones' card draw ability

annotations.description: Using Soul Sear (a premium 5-damage removal spell) to kill a 1/1 Burglar Rat is a massive waste of resources. Soul Sear should be saved for significant threats like large creatures, bombs, or planeswalkers. The Burglar Rat has already triggered its ETB discard effect and is just a 1/1 body that poses minimal threat. Additionally, casting Soul Sear here uses all 3 available mana during combat, preventing any main phase 2 plays. The player has Takenuma Bleeder (3/3) in hand which could have been cast instead and would easily outclass the Burglar Rat in combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Soul Sear targeting Burglar Rat (1/1) during combat, spending 3 mana on removing a minimal threat.
annotations.betterLine: Pass combat without casting Soul Sear, then in main phase 2 cast Takenuma Bleeder or Infernal Idol with the 3 available mana. Save Soul Sear for a real threat like a large creature or bomb.

annotations.description: Cast Wight of Precinct Six (currently only a 2/2 with 1 creature in opponent's graveyard) before playing a land. Should have played a land first (Swamp) to have 4 mana available, which opens up casting two 2-drops (Tinybones + Wight) or Phyrexian Rager for guaranteed card advantage. Additionally, Phyrexian Rager provides immediate card draw which is more reliably valuable than Wight's conditional growth.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wight of Precinct Six without playing a land first
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast both Tinybones, Trinket Thief and Wight of Precinct Six for two bodies on 4 mana, or cast Phyrexian Rager for immediate card advantage with 1 mana held up

annotations.description: Herald's Horn provides weak value here — the deck lacks strong tribal synergies, and the chosen creature type will have limited hits. Meanwhile, Infernal Idol would tap for {B}, enabling a turn 5 Renegade Demon (4 lands + Idol = 5 mana sources) and offering card draw later. Takenuma Bleeder would also be reasonable as a 3/3 body to contest the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Herald's Horn, which provides a minor cost reduction and a weak upkeep trigger with limited tribal density.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first, then cast Infernal Idol to ramp into Renegade Demon next turn. Alternatively, cast Takenuma Bleeder for immediate board presence against the opponent's 2/2 Wight.

annotations.description: Cast Tinybones, Trinket Thief as a 1/2 body with no way to trigger its discard-dependent card draw ability. There are no discard effects on board or in hand (Burglar Rat is in the graveyard), so Tinybones is essentially a vanilla 1/2. Phyrexian Rager would have provided an immediate card draw and a 2/2 body.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Mountain or Swamp), then cast Phyrexian Rager for immediate card advantage and a better body. Tinybones could be held for a future turn when paired with a discard effect, or simply isn't worth the slot without synergy.

annotations.description: MiniMx Dreamer declined to block with Takenuma Bleeder despite it being able to kill Wight of Precinct Six (2/2) while surviving as a 3/1. This let both attackers through for 3 damage and left a scaling threat (Wight) on the board. The Bleeder's 1 life loss trigger is a small cost compared to removing a growing creature for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block, taking 3 damage from Wight (2) and Tinybones (1) while leaving both creatures alive.
annotations.betterLine: Block Wight of Precinct Six with Takenuma Bleeder. Bleeder survives at 3/1, Wight dies, and you only take 1 damage from Tinybones + 1 life from Bleeder's trigger (2 total), while permanently removing a scaling threat.

annotations.description: At 13 life facing 7 damage from attackers (Takenuma Bleeder 3/3 + two Minotaur 2/3 tokens), passing on Rush of Adrenaline before blocks means worse combat outcomes. Using Rush on Wight of Precinct Six (making it 4/3) to block and kill Takenuma Bleeder would save the Wight, kill a real creature (adding to opponent's graveyard to permanently buff Wight), and reduce incoming damage significantly compared to any block configuration without Rush.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Rush of Adrenaline before declaring blockers.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Rush of Adrenaline on Wight of Precinct Six, then block Takenuma Bleeder with the 4/3 Wight — killing the Bleeder, keeping Wight alive, and taking only 2-4 damage instead of a worse outcome.

annotations.description: MiniMx Dreamer has lethal on board (two 2/3 Minotaurs + 3/3 Takenuma Bleeder = 7 damage vs opponent at 6 life with both creatures tapped). Sacrificing Infernal Idol to draw 2 cards and lose 2 life is wasteful — it costs 2 life unnecessarily and consumes mana that could be used to cast Renegade Demon (3BB) as a backup threat if the opponent has removal. Tapping Idol for {B} instead would preserve the option to cast Renegade Demon post-combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Infernal Idol to draw 2 cards and lose 2 life during upkeep
annotations.betterLine: Don't sacrifice the Idol — either tap it for {B} or leave it alone. Attack with all three creatures for 7 damage (lethal). If removal is a concern, keep mana open to cast Renegade Demon (3BB) post-combat as backup using Idol's {B} + Swamp + 3 Mountains.
